skill.name: graphql-schema
skill.description: Patterns for GraphQL queries, mutations, fragments, Apollo Client hooks, and generated TypeScript types.
skill.summary: Create typed GraphQL operations with .gql files, generated hooks, and consistent Apollo Client UI handling.
skill.author: ChrisWiles

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, GraphQL examples, TypeScript examples, and GraphQL field names. I confirmed a limited external-command risk because the skill instructs agents to run npm code generation and schema sync scripts. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or hidden malicious behavior was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to inspect package scripts and ask the user before running GraphQL type generation commands.

remediation.issue: Schema sync command may perform network or local script actions
remediation.suggestion: Document expected schema sync behavior and require confirmation before running any schema download command.

content.value_statement: GraphQL features often drift when queries, generated types, and UI state handling are inconsistent. This skill gives repeatable patterns for .gql files, Apollo hooks, mutation feedback, and code generation.
actual_capabilities: Shows a project layout for .gql operation files and generated TypeScript outputs.
Guides creation of GraphQL queries, mutations, and reusable fragments.
Defines Apollo Client usage with generated hooks and query options.
Specifies mutation UI handling for loading, success, error, and disabled states.
Documents when to run GraphQL type generation after operation changes.
limitations: Does not include a GraphQL schema parser or generator.
Assumes the project already uses Apollo Client and GraphQL code generation.
Does not validate server schema compatibility by itself.
Requires user review before running project npm scripts.

use_cases.title: Add a typed query view
use_cases.description: Create a query file, generate types, and use the generated hook with loading, error, and empty states.

use_cases.title: Ship a safe mutation flow
use_cases.description: Add mutation operations with required error handling, success feedback, loading state, and duplicate-submit protection.

use_cases.title: Standardize GraphQL conventions
use_cases.description: Apply consistent file placement, generated hooks, fragments, and anti-pattern checks across a frontend codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic query
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for adding a new read-only screen.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GraphQL query pattern for [screen name]. Include the .gql file location, generated hook usage, and loading, error, and empty states.

prompt_templates.title: Add a mutation flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for form submission work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GraphQL mutation flow for [action]. Include the mutation file, generated hook usage, disabled submit state, success feedback, and onError behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor inline GraphQL
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for replacing an anti-pattern.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor the inline GraphQL operation in [component or file]. Move it to a .gql file, use generated hooks, and describe the typegen step to run after review.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a GraphQL feature set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for multi-operation feature planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the GraphQL operations for [feature]. Include queries, mutations, fragments, cache update strategy, optimistic update guidance, and risks before running codegen.

output_examples.input: Create a list query for items with pagination.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan that creates a query file, runs type generation after review, imports the generated hook, and handles loading, error, and empty states.

output_examples.input: Add a create item mutation to an existing form.
output_examples.output: A mutation workflow with a dedicated operation file, generated mutation hook, disabled submit button, loading feedback, success notification, and error notification.

output_examples.input: Review a component that uses inline GraphQL.
output_examples.output: A refactor checklist that moves the operation into a .gql file, replaces raw hooks with generated hooks, and identifies the type generation step.

best_practices: Keep GraphQL operations in .gql files and consume generated hooks in components.
Run type generation only after reviewing the project script that will execute.
Give every mutation clear loading, success, and error behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not inline GraphQL literals inside components.
Do not trigger mutations without an onError handler.
Do not allow mutation buttons to stay active while a request is loading.

faq.question: What projects fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It fits TypeScript frontend projects that use GraphQL, Apollo Client, and generated operation types.

faq.question: Does it generate GraphQL schema files?
faq.answer: No. It guides operation patterns and code generation workflows, but it does not generate a server schema.

faq.question: Can it help with mutations?
faq.answer: Yes. It defines mutation files, generated hooks, error handling, success feedback, and loading states.

faq.question: Does it support reusable fragments?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to define fragments and reuse them across GraphQL operations.

faq.question: Should commands run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review project scripts first, then ask for confirmation before running npm type generation commands.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
